Subject: Optimize toolkit — initial packaging questions

Hi Diego,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Two follow-ups from our side as we evaluate Redwood's Optimize toolkit for our inference stack:

1) Packaging — we need clarity on what’s included in the Optimize SKU vs add-ons. Specifically: batching/caching guidance, quantization recommendations, and whether model conversion support is part of the base price.
2) Pricing/discounting — we’re looking at a 12–18 month procurement window. Rough ballpark: ~$120k–$180k annual spend on Inference. Curious what tiers/credits or committed-discount structure you’d recommend.
3) Onboarding — does the package include hands-on sessions (SE time) to enable batch/caching policies and quantization testing?

Could you send a simple breakdown (line items) and any suggested commitment tiers? Procurement would like an option that bundles professional enablement + some credits.

Best,
Sofia Moreno
Head of ML Ops
Streamline Biotech

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Optimize toolkit — initial packaging questions

Hi Sofia — really appreciate the clear asks, and great to meet the team yesterday.

Short answers up front:
- Optimize base SKU includes guidance docs, model/quant profiles (recommended quantization levels by model and sequence length), and an automated suggestions engine for batching and cache settings.
- Hands-on SE time is available as part of an onboarding add-on (2–8 hours, depending on complexity) or included at modest levels for committed deals.
- We can offer tiered committed credits with step-down unit pricing and a one-time onboarding credit.

I attached a light primer that outlines common packaging options and a starter mutual action plan (MA_plan.xlsx) you can share with procurement.

Key technical notes that are often helpful:
- Quantization: for Llama-family-like models we recommend Q8 (per our testing) for production quality/cost tradeoffs. For very latency-sensitive paths we can test Q4f16 on a canary subset.
- Batching: for short-chat-style queries (<=128 tokens) we see best throughput gains with continuous batching windows of 20–50ms and dynamic batch sizes up to 64; prefix/KV caching yields 12–25% token savings on recurring prompts.

Suggested commercial starting point (proposal):
- 12-month committed credits $120k: 15% committed discount + $15k onboarding credits + 25k free runtime credits
- 24-month committed credits $210k: 22% committed discount + $25k onboarding credits + 60k free runtime credits

If you’d like, I can put together a short SOW and a refined pricing sheet. Are you available early next week for a quick call to walk procurement through the MA and onboarding options?

Regards,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
diego_fernandez@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

Folks — forwarding Sofia's ask and the high-level proposal I sent. Procurement is pushing for bundled SE time and a clearer statement of quantization guarantees.

What I want to validate before I send a formal counter:
- Can we include 2 hours of SE onboarding (remote) in the 12-month $120k package without requiring a separate PO?
- Do we feel comfortable recommending Q8 as the default with an explicit note that Q4f16 requires a brief validation window and is subject to model/regression checks?
- Any flexibility on adding an extra 10k runtime credits at 12-month commit to close faster?

Grace — can you confirm rough SE availability and whether we can commit 2 hours as part of the deal?
Lauren — if the customer pushes for an additional 10k credits, what concession budget do you want me to use?

Thanks —
Diego
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Feb 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Internal: Streamline request — recommended commercial and technical approach

Diego — agree with the approach. Quick answers:
- SE onboarding: we can include a 2-hour remote session for the 12-month $120k commitment as a standard concession. Anything more than 4 hours should be scoped and billed.
- Quantization: Q8 is fine to recommend; include language that any lower-bit experiments (Q4f16) will be a short pilot and rollback is supported if quality drops.
- Credits concession: we can add 10k additional runtime credits under a one-off approval. Use deal-level discretionary budget up to 8% of ARR for this early-stage account. If they ask for more, escalate to Sean.

I attached a draft SOW that ties the onboarding hours to specific deliverables (policy tuning for batching, cache rules, and a quantization-dev checklist).

Lauren
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Sofia — thanks for the patience while we aligned internally. Below is a concise, actionable offer you can share with procurement. If this looks good I’ll push the MA/SOW and DocuSign links.

Offer summary (12-month committed credits)
- Committed spend: $120,000 for 12 months
- Commercial: 18% off standard list (applies to consumed runtime units)
- Credits & onboarding: $15,000 in onboarding credits (applies to SE time) + 35,000 runtime credits added up front
- SE support: 2-hour remote onboarding session (policy tuning: continuous batching windows, dynamic batch sizing, prefix/KV cache rules) included
- Technical recommendations included in the package: Q8 quantization as default for production; short Q4f16 pilot available on a per-model basis; expected token savings from prefix caching: 12–20% (pilot-dependent)
- Conditions: pilot of Q4f16 or custom kernel work requires a short validation window and will be scoped in the SOW. Additional SE time available at standard rates or as pre-purchased blocks.

Next steps:
1) If procurement is comfortable, sign the MA (I’ll send DocuSign link) — we can enable the credits and schedule the onboarding session within 5 business days of signature.
2) For the Q4f16 pilot we’ll request a non-production dataset and agree on quality/regression metrics before starting.

Links: HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/rdw-2026-492
DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/links/streamline-maap-sign

If you want to tighten the commercial (e.g., additional runtime credits or longer included SE time) we can discuss a revised 24-month commitment.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this to contract.
